q: The Krylov–Bogoliubov theorem guarantees that every continuous map on a compact metric space has:
opts: At least one invariant Borel probability measure
exp: Krylov–Bogoliubov: take any point x, form the Cesàro averages μₙ = (1/n)∑δ_{fᵏ(x)}, and take a weak-* limit. Compactness of the space (Prokhorov's theorem) ensures a convergent subsequence whose limit is f-invariant.
